title: Capstone: the sphere through local primitives and integration
promptMarkdown: Write a complete connected account of the Čech–de Rham theorem, illustrated on $S^2$. (a) Verify that the four tetrahedral hemispheres in the lesson form a good cover with all triple intersections nonempty and empty fourfold intersection. Compute the two coboundary ranks and all cover cohomology groups. (b) Establish the comparison via the double complex: prove row acyclicity by the partition homotopy, state the column exactness supplied by Poincaré, specify the total sign, and explain the finite elimination argument. For a closed two-form $\sigma$, describe local one-form primitives $\eta_i$, overlap functions $f_{ij}$, and the constant triple-overlap cocycle they produce; show its class is independent of the choices. (c) Compute $\int_{S^2}\Omega$, prove $\Omega$ is not exact, and identify the real cohomology generator. State which inputs are proved in this course, which covering result is assumed for a general manifold, and why this real theorem does not identify integer torsion.
hintLadder: Build the nerve from which intersections are nonempty and contractible.
For a triangle cocycle use vertex 0 to reconstruct vertex potentials.
Track local primitives: closed 2-form → local 1-forms → overlap functions → triple constants.
The partition homotopy resolves one direction, Poincaré resolves the other; use the total sign before claiming a complex.
A nonzero integral on a closed oriented manifold obstructs exactness.
